exactBlocker: Global publishability is decided before product scope is applied. loadPeopleSiteContext returns inactive (catalog-not-publishable) unless every global blocker is zero. Enabling PEOPLE_EBOOK_PREVIEW only creates preview=true; assessEbookPeopleReadiness explicitly refuses ready=true for that context.
unsafeShortcut: Do not force active=true/preview=false on the global catalog or remove the preview guard. Selected canonical records contain facts from every merged chapter/book. A ready Jinshu could then display unaudited outside-book birth/death, names, roles, descriptions and family facts. The local readiness function also relies on upstream global editorial/coverage gates that are not restated per chapter.

references.claim: Module-global PEOPLE_EBOOK comes from loadPeopleSiteContext; product selection occurs later.
Loader reads and checks generation-matched global catalog/site index; lines44-47 use global publishability or explicit preview.
Global blockers are pending date audits, missing/legacy chapters and people, proposed translation repairs, unresolved identity candidate blocks.
Publishability requires nonempty people, catalog.complete===true, and zero global blockers.
Inactive global context returns before product-local readiness can qualify it.
Local checks cover chapter presence, older prompt version and audited/version1 date status, then select canonical people and needs-review flags.
Even locally passing products cannot be ready from preview context; preview can only activate a non-ready glossary.
Site-index chapter records contain book/chapter, promptVersion, dateAudit and mentions; pending editorial repairs are not a chapter-local readiness field.
canonicalRecord constructs names, preferred name/description, roles, claims and life buckets from every cluster member across books.
Canonical identity needs-review flags come from unresolved identity and legacy-member conditions; they are not a per-source editorial/date certificate.
Compiler derives global resolution graph and unresolved candidate state before creating canonical records.
Pending translation repair count and publication completeness are calculated over the whole corpus.
buildEbookPeople filters canonical people by product membership but keeps each selected canonical record whole.
Glossary mentions are filtered to product scope, but family display pulls targets from global PEOPLE_EBOOK.peopleById.
Glossary entry renders global person description, life summary, roles, aliases and family facts; filtering references alone does not isolate provenance.
Generator reports inactive glossary or ready/preview QA separately from ebook construction; it can build an ebook without an active glossary.
Required-glossary QA rejects inactive and preview output; its explicit comment says it verifies report structure, not independent claim qualification or EPUB provenance.
Require-people-glossary mode additionally checks current date audits for manifest-derived scope.
Validator checks required glossary readiness plus entry/index/link/backlink/snippet counts.
Authoritative product scope and ordered chapter list must match manifest; current-date helper validates every product chapter.
Applied-editorial validator enforces reviewed repair history and rejects an extractor reviewing its own editorial proposals.
Validated corpus loading checks each extraction against a fresh chapter packet and authoritative source coverage.
Existing regression deliberately forbids locally complete products from promoting globally incomplete preview data.

pureCanonicalFunctionEvidence.method: Import only the exact canonical standalone publication/readiness module strings through in-memory data URLs. Synthetic locally ready Jinshu fixture plus one missing unrelated chapter; no filesystem corpus reads or mutation.

smallestSafeDesign.recommendation: Add a separate scope-qualified ebook publication context, leaving the global site loader and global completeness contract unchanged. To make Jinshu-only gates sufficient, compile rendered facts from Jinshu scope rather than filtering whole globally aggregated person records.
steps: Use authoritative ordered ebook manifest scope (all 130 Jinshu chapters for a complete Jinshu product); never derive required coverage from successful extraction/index entries. Keep explicit volume scope if a product is a volume.

Keep the fresh global identity graph and accepted conservative resolution decisions for canonical IDs and ambiguity checks. Any unresolved review pair touching a Jinshu local/canonical person still blocks that product, including outside-book homonyms; a validated possible-same-as preserves separate people.

Reuse canonical record construction on only scoped factual members/claims, while retaining their globally resolved canonical IDs. Scope every rendered source-derived field: preferred label/override support, aliases, descriptions, roles, life facts and age derivations, family edges/inverses, and references. Preserve claim/evidence provenance; do not trim only references from a full global canonical record.

Build family edges and derived inverse relationships from scoped source facts after projection. Resolve every rendered target from scoped supported people; if an explicitly imported outside-scope label/fact is required, add its exact source chapters as gated dependencies rather than silently importing it.

Require fresh production extraction validation and complete current prompt coverage, zero pending translation proposals, valid independent applied-editorial history, current independently approved date reports and reference evidence, and no relevant unresolved identity pairs. Do not change report hashes, accepted source/extraction pins, or independence rules.

Write a distinct versioned scope manifest/certificate and matching catalog/site-index generation through existing generated-data shard loaders/writers. Record authoritative scope, source/extraction/decision fingerprints, gate evidence and identity-generation identity. Do not set the global catalog complete flag.

Load that context per ebook product, not from the current module-global PEOPLE_EBOOK. Pass its context into chapter links and family rendering so global person lookup cannot leak back into scoped output. Cache by exact scope/fingerprints if needed.

Feed the certified non-preview context to existing readiness/rendering. Strengthen scope loading to reject missing or invalid prompt versions and count metadata. Validate current scope certificate plus existing required-glossary EPUB/link/mention/backlink checks before publication; QA sidecars alone are not gate evidence.
smallestSafeDesign.whyNotOnlyReadinessChange: The existing local readiness predicate has no pending-translation-repair count, independent applied-editorial history, or per-fact provenance projection. Its safety depends on the upstream global gate. Changing a boolean would remove that protection.
smallestSafeDesign.smallerButConditionalAlternative: If retaining globally aggregated facts is preferred, gate the complete dependency closure of every rendered person/name/life/family fact. That can permit unrelated books to remain incomplete, but Jinshu-only approval is insufficient when its displayed records depend on unaudited outside-book chapters. It does not fully deliver independent Jinshu release cadence.

meaningfulTestsNeeded: Complete scoped Jinshu plus unrelated missing/unaudited/unresolved other-book data publishes a required glossary; the global website remains gated and the existing preview-promotion test continues to reject raw global preview.
Authoritative complete-book scope detects a missing Jinshu chapter, a skipped chapter, duplicates/reordering, and forged product/QA scope; explicit volume products cannot claim whole-book completion.

Each Jinshu gate independently blocks: legacy/missing prompt metadata, stale source/extraction, pending translation repair, rejected repair applied, invalid editorial history or same-context editorial review, unaudited/failed/stale date report, stale secondary references, and relevant unresolved identity pair.

Unresolved same-name pair against an outside-book person still blocks Jinshu; unrelated outside-book unresolved pairs do not. Reviewed possible-same-as keeps its two people separate and never merges them.

Global shared canonical person has an outside-book-only birth date, alias, role, descriptor and family edge from an unaudited chapter; none leak into the scoped rendered entry. Its canonical ID and in-book supported facts/links remain stable.

Outside-source-only preferred-name override or inverse family fact either becomes an explicit fully gated dependency or fails scoped support checks; unresolved/missing family targets fail rather than disappear.

Mismatched scope/generation/prompt version, missing scope certificate, modified source/extraction/editorial/resolution/date evidence after compilation, or altered artifact hashes fail freshness checks.
Real EPUB required-glossary integration verifies every expected person, index target, English mention link, Chinese/English source snippet and backlink; no links target removed global entries.
PEOPLE_EBOOK_PREVIEW and allow-preview cannot satisfy required-glossary mode. A forged ready QA sidecar cannot replace a current scope certificate and current date/identity/editorial gates.
Global publication behavior and fully complete-corpus ebook behavior remain unchanged; no re-extraction, paid runner, automatic identity relaxation or approval-hash rewriting is introduced.
limits: Architecture only. No code implementation, canonical data, generated catalog build, deployment, or model calls were performed.
No statement that Jinshu currently passes all gates; this investigates what would happen if those scoped gates passed.
The corpus-wide resolution graph must remain current for identities used by the book; this design does not waive relevant cross-book identity review.
